title: This BEMT Sunscreen Is the Most Invisible SPF We’ve Tried—You Won’t Even Realize You Have It On - Glamour

 We tried out the new BEMT SPF 50 on four different skin tones and types. By Alanna Martine Kilkeary November 19, 2026 Courtesy of brands; Alanna Martine Kilkeary, Danielle James, Emily Tannenbaum, Jenny Berg; Glamour composite by Jemeria Davison Welcome to Just My Type, a monthly series in which Glamour editors test-drive the latest and greatest in makeup, hair care, and skin care. No one has time for products that work against their natural features, so we try them across a range of skin tones, skin types, and hair textures. In this month’s installment, our editors review La Roche Posay’s newest sunscreen launch. Read on to find out if it was just our type, because it might just be yours too. 
 There might be a lot of reasons why you’re less than thrilled to apply sunscreen every day. Maybe you have sensitive skin that doesn’t play well with most SPF formulas. Or you have a darker skin tone and can’t find anything that doesn’t leave a chalky cast behind. No matter your gripe with sunscreen, there’s no escaping the fact that dermatologists say it’s the most important skin care product in your entire routine. Unfortunately the US has limited options on the formulas available to consumers because the FDA regulates SPF as a drug, meaning rigorous approval is needed before introducing any of the new filters that have been available for years in Europe, Australia, and Asia.
 But all that changed this year, when the FDA approved a filter called bemotrizinol (BEMT). It’s been used for decades overseas and boasts broad-spectrum protection as well as a so-light-it’s-basically-lotion feel. And it won’t create a cast on melanated skin. The first SPF with BEMT on American shelves is the new La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense Sunscreen (SPF 50) . We got our hands on it to see for ourselves what all the fuss is about. Here, four different editors test out UVDefense and share how well it wore on various skin tones, andunder makeup, and whether it felt greasy, stingy, or just plain annoying like other formulas they’ve tried (Spoiler alert: It did not).

 About the formula
 First, let’s talk about what makes this formula so special. It’s one of the first FDA-approved sunscreens that features the filter bemotrizinol (a.k.a. BEMT) in the US. What makes this filter unique is that it shields against both UVA and UVB rays, is extremely lightweight (to the point that you’ll second guess if you applied anything), and disappears into skin with zero cast. The formula also features standout antioxidants to help protect skin from further damage and oxidative stress. It’s oil-free, noncomedogenic (so it won’t seep into pores), and fragrance-free (so safe for sensitive skin types). All that and it delivers SPF 50 sun protection.
 The texture is lightweight and milky at first (almost runny), and it disappears when applied onto skin. There’s barely any massaging or rubbing in needed. It’s totally weightless, with no residue, so you can apply foundation , tinted moisturizer , blush, or any other makeup product on top without fear of transfer or smudging—it’s as if it isn’t even there.
 The Reviews
 Alanna Martine Kilkeary , commerce writer

 Original video from Alanna Martine Kilkeary testing La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense Sunscreen (SPF 50) Skin type: Combination and acne-prone
 SPF history: Wears sunscreen every single day, under makeup.
 Typical concerns with SPF: Not blending well with makeup; making oily spots more greasy
 TL;DR: Alanna loves how well this formula wears under makeup, and how easy it is to incorporate into her daily skin care routine. It never skips, pills, or makes skin feel gross—instead, it makes your complexion feel soft and plush.
 How it felt: “This pick has a milky texture that glides onto skin and melts quickly for a supremely smooth finish—especially beneficial for my acne-prone skin type.”
 How it looked: “It turns practically invisible once blended in, so no white cast or residue. Fair warning, the texture looks very runny at first but actually blends down into seemingly nothing. It’s kind of amazing because it’s the total opposite of a lot of sunscreens I grew up applying (that took nearly ten minutes to fully rub into my skin).”
 Original photo from Alanna Martine Kilkeary testing La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense Sunscreen (SPF 50) Original photo from Alanna Martine Kilkeary testing La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense Sunscreen (SPF 50) How it wore: “After testing it for a couple weeks, I didn’t see any new breakouts crop up either—a personal victory for me, as a lot of sunscreens tend to give me pimples. I like that it’s fragrance-free and pairs well under makeup. My skin is plump and soft post-application, with a touch of dew, but nongreasy or shiny.”
 Add to routine? “I’ll definitely be using this on a regular basis. This one is a true multitasker: SPF, moisturizer, and primer all in one.”
 Emily Tannenbaum , contributing editor
 Courtesy of brand

 Original video from Emily Tannenbaum testing La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense Sunscreen SPF 50 Skin type: Combination, sensitive
 SPF history: Very diligent with sunscreen; only use SPF 50 or above; particularly obsessed with Korean Sunscreens like Dr. Althea .
 Usual concerns with SPF: Greasy textures, off-putting smells, makeup pilling
 TL;DR: Despite an initial greasy texture, the formula melted into Emily”s skin beautifully, leaving her feeling hydrated and acting as a great base for her makeup.
 How it felt: “ Korean sunscreens have spoiled me when it comes to their moisturizer-like textures, so I was slightly put off when I applied this slippery formula to my forehead, where my skin is the most oily. Thankfully, that initial greasy feeling quickly subsided as the product melted into my skin and dried down.”
 How it looked: “It left my skin looking plump and and radiant, not shiny.”
 Original photo from Emily Tannenbaum testing La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense Sunscreen SPF 50 Original photo from Emily Tannenbaum testing La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense Sunscreen SPF 50 How it wore: “Despite the initial greasy feeling, the formula ultimately felt hydrating and light on my skin. Of course, the test wasn’t over. After applying my everyday makeup routine, I can happily confirm this sunscreen acted as the perfect base without pilling or causing my foundation to slip in any way.”
 Add to routine? “Yes. I’d definitely encourage US sunscreen skeptics to give this a shot, one tough customer to another.”
 Danielle Jackson , Glamour contributor
 Courtesy of brand 
 La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense Sunscreen (SPF 50)
 $40 Amazon
 $40 La Roche Posay
 Original video from Danielle Jackson testing La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense Sunscreen SPF 50 Skin type: Combination
 SPF history: Wears sunscreen every day whether directly in the sun or not or, and even if it's cloudy or overcast (but she says she could probably do a better job of remembering to reapply)
 Usual concerns with SPF: Leaves behind a cast; pilling
 TL;DR: Danielle found this sunscreen to be mattifying and free of a whitish cast. She likes how lightweight it feels and how it doesn’t take much to fully absorb.
 How it felt: “With a milky-but-not-runny texture that doesn’t pill or separate when I rub it in, I don’t need to use a lot of it to feel like I’m covering my whole face.”
 How it looked: “When I’m choosing a sunscreen, I’m usually looking for a formula that doesn’t make me look ghostly but that also can protect and moisturize my skin at the same time. On the flip side, it also can’t make my T-zone appear even oilier than it already is. After previously being disappointed by an Anthelios sunscreen that left my skin with a slightly purple tint, I’ve been using this sunscreen every day for nearly two weeks (with no white cast!), and I have to say I’m surprised by how much I like it.”
 Original photo from Danielle Jackson testing La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense Sunscreen SPF 50 Original photo from Danielle Jackson testing La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense Sunscreen SPF 50 How it wore: “Even when I layer my foundation, concealer, and powder over it, it never feels like there’s an overwhelming amount of product just sitting on my face.”
 Add to routine? “This one gets a 10 from me, and I’d definitely recommend it.”
 Jenny Berg , Glamour contributor

 Original video from Jenny Berg testing La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense Sunscreen (SPF 50) Skin type: Combination and dry
 SPF history: Wears sunscreen every day—not only because she’s fair-skinned, but because of a family history of skin cancer; burns easily, so if she’s in the sun, SPF is a nonnegotiable
 Usual concerns with SPF: Causing breakouts, not playing well with makeup products
 TL;DR: Jenny liked how velvety soft the formula is and how moisturized her skin felt after the fact. She nerded out over the novel SPF filter it boasts and would recommend it if you’re looking for a formula that won’t leave behind a white cast or residue.
 How it felt: “When I first started applying the sunscreen, I thought, Ooh, it’s soft! And glide-y! (This was pre-coffee, so my brain wasn’t forming adult words yet, I suppose!) The texture is silky and lightweight, and it feels soothing and a little cooling on the skin. My skin didn’t feel noticeably softer, per se, but it did feel nice and moisturized.”
 How it looked: “I looked remarkably dewy (one could even say... shiny) after applying it.”
 Original photo from Jenny Berg testing La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense Sunscreen (SPF 50) Original photo from Jenny Berg testing La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense Sunscreen (SPF 50) How it wore: “Though the formula is lightweight, it took a little time (maybe two minutes) to dry down a bit, and it still felt a bit tacky to the touch when I started to put on makeup. (What can I say; I was in a rush.) I thought the makeup might pill, but it slid on easily and evenly over the SPF.”
 Add to routine? “I would recommend this—in part, I confess, because of the novelty. I was on a trip with fellow beauty writers last month, and everyone was passing around a BEMT formula like it was a new baby they wanted to meet. (A new filter is big news for us beauty nerds!) Also, as I said, this has a really nice silky texture and layers well under makeup. Plus, I know that derms love LRP in general, especially for sensitive skin—and this has that good old Cell-Ox Shield technology, which pairs the sun filter with antioxidants.”
 Alanna Martine Kilkeary is Glamour's commerce writer. She has over seven years of freelance and editing experience in beauty content, including makeup and skincare testing and reviewing, gifting and shopping.
